'''Luke Cameron Harangody''' (born January 2, 1988) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Club Joventut Badalona|Divina Seguros Joventut]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]]. He completed his college career at the [[University of Notre Dame]] in 2010. He is the only men's player in the history of the [[Big East Conference]] to average 20 points and 10 rebounds per game in conference play for his career.<ref name="2010 Big East">{{cite press release |url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030710aab.html |title=Luke Harangody And Tim Abromaitis Garner All-BIG EAST Conference Honors |publisher=University of Notre Dame |date=March 7, 2010 |access-date=March 18, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110617025714/http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030710aab.html |archive-date=June 17, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was the 2008 [[Big East Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Player of the Year]],<ref name="Awards">{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/basketball/ncaa/wires/03/11/2060.ap.bkc.big.east.awards.0300/ |title=Notre Dame's Harangody and Brey sweep Big East postseason awards |publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=March 11, 2008 |access-date=October 13, 2008 }}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> and was named to the second team on the 2008 [[Associated Press]] [[2008 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-America]] team.<ref name="2008 All-America">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=3322266 |title=For first time in six decades, no seniors on AP All-America team |publisher=ESPN |date=March 31, 2008 |access-date=December 29, 2010}}</ref> He is also the first Notre Dame men's player to be a three-time first-team All-Big East selection (and just 11th overall) (2008–2010), and the first men's player to lead the conference in both scoring and rebounding in consecutive seasons (2008 and 2009).<ref name="2010 Big East" />

Harangody considered entering the [[2009 NBA draft]], but withdrew his name to return to Notre Dame for his senior season.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/college/2009/06/20/2009-06-20_luke_harangody_withdraws.html | location=New York | work=Daily News | title=Luke Harangody withdraws from NBA Draft, returns to Irish with chip on shoulder | first=Dick | last=Weiss | date=June 20, 2009}}</ref> Harangody ended his Notre Dame career as the only player to have over 2000 points and 1000 rebounds.

== Early years ==
Growing up in [[Schererville, Indiana]], Harangody, the son of a former [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana University football]] player, had an intense [[sibling rivalry]] with his brother Ty, who is 20 months older and was one grade ahead of him in school. The two began with basketball games on a mini-hoop in Harangody's room, which ended when they were kicked out for shaking the light fixtures. The games then moved to a court that their father set up in the basement, and from there to the backyard once they outgrew the basement. Their father soon banned them from the backyard because their one-on-one games almost invariably ended in fistfights, but that only moved their rivalry to local parks. Bigger and stronger, Ty won most of their games; Harangody would later say about those days, "I still look back on that as where most of my competitive nature comes from. To beat him, I'd go all out, all the time." Eventually, the brothers' athletic paths split. Ty followed in their father's footsteps as a football player, eventually earning a [[athletic scholarship|scholarship]] to IU as a [[tight end]]; his career was ended by a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] in his sophomore year. Harangody grew 3 inches as a high school freshman and opted for basketball.<ref name=ESPNRittenberg>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/columns/story?id=3254631 |title= Harangody emerging as Big East's best big man |first=Adam |last=Rittenberg |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=February 27, 2008 |access-date=October 13, 2008}}</ref>

Harangody starred at [[Andrean High School]] in nearby [[Merrillville, Indiana|Merrillville]]. In his last two high school seasons, he averaged over 20 points and 10 rebounds, was named as the top player in Northwest Indiana by at least one media outlet in each season, and received All-State recognition in Indiana in both seasons.<ref name=NDBio>{{cite web |url=http://und.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/harangody_luke00.html |title=Men's Basketball Player Bio: Luke Harangody |publisher=University of Notre Dame Athletic Department |access-date=October 13, 2008 |archive-date=February 21, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090221124557/http://und.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/harangody_luke00.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== College career ==

=== Freshman season ===
Despite Harangody's credentials, he had considerable doubts about his ability to play in the Big East, and much of [[University of Notre Dame|Notre Dame's]] recruitment consisted of convincing him he was good enough to play in the conference.

After a [[double-double]] against [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]] in the second game of the season, Irish head coach [[Mike Brey]] considered adding Harangody to the starting lineup, but Harangody hesitated and Brey decided to wait until Big East play. Harangody would go on to start the team's final 16 games.<ref name=ESPNRittenberg />

Harangody went on to average 11.2 points and 6.2 rebounds that season, and was named to the Big East All-Rookie first team. However, conditioning proved to be a problem for him that season; he gained weight during the season (not typical for college athletes), and he played more than 30 minutes only once as a freshman. His conditioning caught up with him in the [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]]. He played only 17 minutes in Notre Dame's first-round loss to [[Winthrop Eagles men's basketball|Winthrop]], and finished with 4 points and one rebound. About that game, he would later remember that "It was hard to get up and down the court. I hit that wall and there was nothing I could do to get out of it. I never wanted to feel like that again." He then had dinner with his parents shortly after the game, an event which his father clearly remembered in an interview the following season: "On the spot, he says, 'I've got to do something.' He rededicated himself from the minute they lost that game."<ref name=ESPNRittenberg />

=== Sophomore season ===
{{See also|2007–08 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team}}
His rededication began with a change in diet; he and the team's trainer worked on a nutrition program that limited his intake of fried foods and carbohydrates. Harangody also increased the intensity of his workout regimen, in both cardiovascular work and weight training. The work paid off in his sophomore season; his body fat content dropped from 14% at the end of his freshman season to 8% by the end of the 2007–08 season.<ref name=ESPNRittenberg /> Harangody also took more of a leadership role on the team, notably berating several of the team's freshmen for giggling in the locker room after a January 19, 2008, loss to [[2007–08 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]].<ref name=ESPNRittenberg />

Harangody ended the season averaging 20.4 points and 10.6 rebounds,<ref name="ND 2008 stats">{{cite web |url=http://und.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2007-2008/teamcume.html#TEAM.IND |title=2007–08 Notre Dame Men's Basketball: Notre Dame Season Box Score |publisher=University of Notre Dame Athletic Department |access-date=October 13, 2008 |archive-date=July 6, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080706145735/http://und.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2007-2008/teamcume.html#TEAM.IND |url-status=dead }}</ref> which made him the Big East's leading scorer and second-leading rebounder.<ref name="Big East 2008 overall stats">{{cite web |url=http://www.bigeast.org/fls/19400/stats/mbasketball/2007-2008/CONFLDRS.HTM#conf.wki |title=2007–08 BIG EAST Conference Individual Basketball Statistics |publisher=Big East Conference |date=March 30, 2008 |access-date=October 13, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120220013031/http://www.bigeast.org/fls/19400/stats/mbasketball/2007-2008/CONFLDRS.HTM#conf.wki |archive-date=February 20, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In contrast to his early doubts about his ability to play in the Big East, he had even better numbers in Big East play, with averages of 23.3 points and 11.3 rebounds, which led the conference in both categories.<ref name="Big East 2008 conference stats">{{cite web|url=http://www.bigeast.org/fls/19400/stats/mbasketball/2007-2008/CONFONLY.HTM#conf.wki |title=2007–08 BIG EAST Conference Individual Basketball Statistics (Conference games only) |publisher=Big East Conference |date=March 30, 2008 |access-date=October 13, 2008}}</ref> This also made him one of only five players in the previous decade to average 22 points and 11 rebounds in conference play for a [[BCS conference]] team.<ref name=ESPNRittenberg />  His scoring and leadership led the Irish to a 14–4 conference record and 24–7 regular season record.<ref name="ND 2008 stats" /> The Irish also became the first team in Big East men's basketball history to go unbeaten at home in conference play in consecutive seasons.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280650087 |title=Irish become first Big East team to go undefeated at home two straight seasons |agency=Associated Press |work=ESPN.com |date=March 5, 2008 |access-date=October 13, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080311000549/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280650087 |archive-date=March 11, 2008 }}</ref> Although the Irish lost in the first round of the Big East tournament to [[Marquette Golden Eagles|Marquette]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280730087 |title=McNeal's career-high 28 carry Marquette to Big East semis |agency=Associated Press |work=ESPN.com |date=March 13, 2008 |access-date=October 13, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080319104919/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280730087 |archive-date=March 19, 2008 }}</ref> Notre Dame earned their second straight [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] bid as a #5 seed. The Irish beat [[2007–08 George Mason Patriots men's basketball team|George Mason]] in the first round and went out in the second to [[2007–08 Washington State Cougars men's basketball team|Washington State]].

After the season, Harangody was named the conference [[Big East Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Player of the Year]],<ref name="Awards" /> and was also named to the 1st Team All Big East squad.<ref name="All-Big East 2008">{{cite news|url=http://www.bigeast.org/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=19400&ATCLID=1409119 |title=2008 All-BIG EAST Men's Basketball Teams Announced |publisher=Big East Conference |date=March 10, 2008 |access-date=October 13, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081202030849/http://www.bigeast.org/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=19400 |archive-date=December 2, 2008 }}</ref> He was named to the [[Associated Press]]' [[All-America]] Second Team on March 31, 2008.<ref name="2008 All-America" />

=== Junior season ===
{{See also|2008–09 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team}}
[[File:Luke Harangody's head.png|thumb|right|200px|Harangody in his junior year]]
Harangody never considered declaring for the [[2008 NBA draft]]. With Harangody and fellow All-Big East first-teamer<ref name="All-Big East 2008" /> [[Kyle McAlarney]] leading an experienced team, the Irish were expected to make a deep run in the 2009 NCAA Tournament, with [[Dick Vitale]] naming the Irish #6 in his preseason rankings<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/dickvitale/news/story?id=3544438 |title=Dickie V's Preseason Top 40 |first=Dick |last=Vitale |author-link=Dick Vitale |work=ESPN.com |date=September 8, 2008 |access-date=October 13, 2008}}</ref> and [[Andy Katz]] placing the Irish in a "next tier" of teams that he effectively ranked from 8th to 16th.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/columns/story?id=3640708 |title= Tar Heels on top as season sets to begin |first=Andy |last=Katz |author-link=Andy Katz |work=ESPN.com |date=October 13, 2008 |access-date=October 13, 2008}}</ref>

However, Notre Dame had to deal with a possible threat to Harangody's college eligibility during the 2008 offseason. A [[Boston, Massachusetts|Boston]] company, Cellular Services Worldwide, had obtained [[public domain]] photos of Harangody and [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Irish]] [[quarterback]] [[Jimmy Clausen]] and used them in an advertisement on a Notre Dame fan site on the Web. Such a use of images of players is a violation of NCAA rules. The school immediately issued a [[cease and desist]] letter to the company, which satisfied NCAA requirements and ensured the players' eligibility.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://myespn.go.com/blogs/others/0-0-48/Morning-Coffee--Notre-Dame-says-cease-and-desist.html |title=Morning Coffee: Cease and Desist |first=Graham |last=Watson |work=ESPN.com |date=July 23, 2008 |access-date=October 13, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080920105645/http://myespn.go.com/blogs/others/0-0-48/Morning-Coffee--Notre-Dame-says-cease-and-desist.html |archive-date=September 20, 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The Fighting Irish finished a disappointing 21–15, losing in the Final Four of the NIT to Penn State after climbing as high as #7 in the polls during the season.

=== Senior season ===
{{See also|2009–10 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team}}
After declaring for the [[2009 NBA draft]], Harangody withdrew and returned for his senior year at Notre Dame.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Dick|first1=Weiss|title=Luke Harangody withdraws from NBA Draft, returns to Irish with chip on shoulder|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/college/luke-harangody-withdraws-nba-draft-returns-irish-chip-shoulder-article-1.377600|access-date=July 7, 2014|work=nydailynews.com|date=June 20, 2009}}</ref>

The Irish rebounded to reach the Big East semi-finals and the NCAA Tournament.  Harangody was named All-Big East for the third year in a row and the All-American team for the third year in a row, making him the first Notre Dame player to be named an All-American 3 years in a row in basketball since [[Kevin O'Shea (basketball)|Kevin O'Shea]].

== Professional career ==
Harangody was selected by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the 52nd overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. On August 10, 2010, Harangody signed a two-year deal with the Celtics.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/2010/news/08/10/celtics.harangody.ap/index.html?rss=true Celtics sign second-round pick Luke Harangody]</ref>
On November 2, 2010, Harangody made his NBA debut in a game against the [[Detroit Pistons]]. Harangody was 2-of-2 from the field, and scored four points in three minutes of playing time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4276/luke-harangody |title=Luke Harangody Stats, News, Photos – Boston Celtics |publisher=ESPN |date=January 2, 1988 |access-date=December 29, 2010}}</ref>

On January 7, 2011, in a 122–102 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]], Harangody achieved career highs of 17 points, 11 rebounds, and two blocked shots.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/sports/12003215428879/rookie-harangody-leads-celtics-over-raptors/|title=Rookie Harangody leads Celtics over Raptors|publisher=WHDH-TV|date=January 7, 2011|access-date=March 5, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110110231313/http://www1.whdh.com/news/articles/sports/12003215428879/rookie-harangody-leads-celtics-over-raptors|archive-date=January 10, 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Harangody was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on February 24, 2011, along with teammate [[Semih Erden]] in exchange for a second-round draft pick in the 2013 NBA Draft.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cavaliers Acquire Erden and Harangody from Boston for Future Second Round Pick|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/trade_110224.html|access-date=July 7, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=February 24, 2011}}</ref> On January 27, 2012, he debuted in the [[NBA Development League]] for Cleveland's affiliate [[Canton Charge]] with a [[double-double]] of 11 points and a team-high 11 rebounds against the [[Bakersfield Jam]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20120127/CTNBAK/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore|title=Friday, January 27, 2012; 10:00 PM ET – Jam Events Center, Bakersfield, CA|access-date=January 28, 2012|date=January 27, 2012|work=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref> He added a double-double the following night against the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] with a team-high 21 points and 11 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20120128/CTNLAD/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore|title=Saturday, January 28, 2012; 9:30 PM ET – Toyota Sports Center, El Segundo, CA|access-date=January 29, 2012|date=January 28, 2012|work=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref> Harangody was recalled by the Cavaliers on February 1, 2012,<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7529087/cleveland-cavaliers-recall-forward-luke-harangody-d-league Cavaliers recall Luke Harangody]</ref> but reassigned on March 6, 2012.<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/219465/Cavaliers_Assign_Eyenga_Harangody_To_Canton Cavaliers Assign Eyenga, Harangody To Canton]</ref> On July 11, 2012, the Cavaliers signed Harangody to a one-year, $1.1 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/story/19564794/cavaliers-sign-forward-luke-harangody|title=Cavaliers sign forward Luke Harangody|work=CBS Sports|access-date=July 11, 2012}}</ref> Harangody was waived by the Cavaliers on November 29, 2012.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/roster-move-121129 Cavaliers Waive Luke Harangody, Sign Kevin Jones]</ref>

On December 28, 2012, Harangody was acquired by the [[Canton Charge]]. He was then immediately traded to the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] for [[JaJuan Johnson]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/charge_acquire_johnson__1st_r_2012_12_28.html Charge Acquire Johnson & 1st Round Pick From Mad Ants] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160125165703/http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/charge_acquire_johnson__1st_r_2012_12_28.html |date=January 25, 2016 }}</ref>

Harangody joined the [[Denver Nuggets]] for the 2013 Las Vegas Summer League.<ref>{{cite news|title=Denver Nuggets announce 2013 Summer League roster|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-announce-2013-summer-league-roster|access-date=July 7, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2013}}</ref> On August 8, 2013, Harangody signed a one–year deal with the Russian club [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Unics Kazan announced Luke Harangody|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/russia/61125/unics-kazan-announced-luke-harangody.html|publisher=Sportando.net|access-date=August 8, 2013}}</ref>

On July 13, 2014, it was announced that Harangody had signed a two-year contract with the Spanish [[Liga ACB|ACB]] and [[EuroLeague]] club [[Valencia Basket]].<ref>{{Cite news | url = http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/138490/180 | title = Harangody heading to Valencia | work = Euroleague.net | date = July 13, 2014 | access-date= July 13, 2014 }}</ref> On June 22, 2015, he parted ways with Valencia.<ref>{{cite news|title=Valencia parts ways with Serhiy Lishchuk and Luke Harangody|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/165017/valencia-parts-ways-with-serhiy-lishchuk-and-luke-harangody.html|access-date=June 22, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=June 22, 2015}}</ref>
[[File:Harangody - 9.jpeg|thumb|Harangody during his presentation as a [[Valencia Basket]] player]]
In July 2015, Harangody joined the [[Phoenix Suns]] for the 2015 Las Vegas Summer League.<ref>{{cite news|title=Suns Announce 2015 Summer League Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-announce-2015-summer-league-roster|access-date=September 30, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2015}}</ref> On August 5, 2015, he signed with the Turkish club [[Darüşşafaka S.K.|Darüşşafaka]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Luke Harangody signs with Darussafaka Dogus, agent says|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/171787/luke-harangody-signs-with-darussafaka-dogus-agent-says.html|access-date=September 30, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=August 5, 2015}}</ref> On July 21, 2016, he re-signed with Darüşşafaka for one more season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Darussafaka Dogus keep Luke Harangody|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/207136/darussafaka-dogus-keep-luke-harangody.html|access-date=July 13, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=July 21, 2017}}</ref>

On July 14, 2017, Harangody signed with German club [[ratiopharm Ulm]] for the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=NBA-ERFAHRENER BIG MAN ENTSCHEIDET SICH FÜR ULM|url=http://ratiopharm-ulm.com/news-archiv/1974-nba-erfahrener-big-man-entscheidet-sich-fuer-ulm|access-date=July 14, 2017|work=ratiopharm-ulm.com|date=July 14, 2017|language=de|archive-date=August 20, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170820160126/http://ratiopharm-ulm.com/news-archiv/1974-nba-erfahrener-big-man-entscheidet-sich-fuer-ulm|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 31 games played for Ulm (in both the [[Basketball Bundesliga|BBL]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] competitions), he averaged 9.1 points, 5.5 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game.

On October 2, 2018, Harangody returned to Spain for a second stint, signing a one-year deal with [[Club Joventut Badalona|Divina Seguros Joventut]].<ref>{{cite news | title=Luke Harangody signs with Joventut Badalona | url=https://sportando.basketball/en/spain/acb/290398/luke-harangody-signs-with-joventut-badalona.html | access-date=October 2, 2018 | work=Sportando.basketball | date=October 2, 2018 | archive-date=October 4, 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004110503/https://sportando.basketball/en/spain/acb/290398/luke-harangody-signs-with-joventut-badalona.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>
